newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Market perceptions behind cash rate decision-RBNZ.
newsitem.headline: Market perceptions behind cash rate decision-RBNZ.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand explained on Wednesday that it dropped its plan to move to a cash rate policy targeting system because of a weight of market objections over how the system would have been perceived.

In a detailed assessment of why it announced two weeks ago it was dropping the plan, the RBNZ said submissions from the market cast doubt on its idea, "mostly in relation to areas where perceptions are important".

In particular, the bank said, the net gains of the proposed system were outweighed by perceptions of the consequences of more frequent, formal reviews of monetary settings. Also taken into account were perceptions of the effectiveness of the bank's signalling following recent modifications.
The RBNZ said it believed perceptions were important in judging the success of monetary policy.
"As much as anything, it was for this reason that we were keen to seek advice and that we issued the discussion paper.
"Against this background it was decided that there was sufficient uncertainty about the net gains of the proposals to warrant not proceeding to implement the proposed system," the bank added.
Next week's Monetary Policy Statement, due to be released on Friday, is the second of the bank's quarterly policy set pieces of the year.
The set pieces are an opportunity for the bank to express in clear, quantitative terms, the intended state of monetary conditions both now and in the future.
Several submissions from the market into the proposed cash rate system said a change would be unnecessary in view of the existing quantitative signalling method.
More importantly, they said a change could be perceived as counter-productive, the RBNZ added.
The MPS statement is due to be made public at 9.00 a.m. on June 27 (2100 GMT, June 26).

Market observers expect the statement to endorse an easing which has taken place in both short interest rates and the kiwi dollar's Trade Weighted Index (TWI) =NZD since the RBNZ's last formal statement on March 13.
However, opinions are divided over how much of an easing will be approved.
In March the bank said its preferred mix of monetary conditions was 7.50 percent for the 90-day bank bill rate and 68.0 for the TWI.
On Wednesday afternoon the bill rate was 60 basis points below that target level at 6.90 percent and the TWI stood at 67.54.

According to the bank's calculation of the degree of easing contained in those two elements -- forming the so-called Monetary Conditions Index NZ/MCI -- the market has built in an easing of 94 basis points at present.
Economists' expectations of the net easing to be approved by RBNZ next week range from 50 to 100 basis points, with some looking to a possible 150 b.p..
